conviction_note: Sum of four findings that point both ways: a record-heat tailwind into the indoor-entertainment quarter and the quarter after it (+2.5), offset by the fact that the -4% comp anchor everyone is trading off was set four days into a 39-day North American World Cup that a direct LBE peer has since blamed for its own June (-2.0), plus two smaller positives from the credit documents and the August incentive grants; net is a modest positive tilt against a +6.18 skew that is paying for a credit accident I could not find evidence of.

findings.finding: NOAA's summer summary, published three trading days before this print, makes June-August 2026 the warmest summer for the contiguous US in the 132-year record (74.4F, +3.0F above average) with August 2026 the warmest August ever recorded (75.6F, daytime max 88.6F) - June and July sit inside D&B's fiscal Q2 (May 6 - Aug 4) and August sits in the Q3 quarter-to-date that management will be asked about on the call, and air-conditioned eatertainment is the category that gains share from record heat.
findings.why_not_priced: Weather is not an aggregated financial datum - there is no estimate-revision line, no Zacks field and no wire item that carries it into a Q2 model. NOAA's release landed 2026-09-09/10 (CNN's URL path /2026/09/09/ dates it independently) and PLAY spent that window making a new 52-week low: if the market had connected a 132-year demand record to the quarter being reported, the 25-delta skew would not be +6.18 with downside bid and the stock would not be 18.35% lower over 20 days. The Q3-QTD leg matters more than the printed quarter for this name - its two biggest up-prints (+17.74% Jun-2025, +16.07% Mar-2026) were about forward comp trajectory, not the quarter in hand.
findings.independence: Lucky Strike Entertainment's FY26 Q4 release (2026-08-27) says venue momentum 'returned immediately' once the World Cup ended in mid-July, i.e. inside D&B's quarter and before the record-heat August - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1840572/000162828026059178/pressreleaseq4fy-26.htm . Note this is the same document that sources finding 2, in the opposite direction; treat the pair as one source cluster.

findings.finding: The '-4% quarter-to-date' comp figure the whole consensus is anchored on was given on the 2026-06-15 Q1 call - four days into the 2026 North American World Cup (June 11 - July 19), a 39-day window that falls entirely inside D&B's fiscal Q2 and covers roughly 5 of its 13 weeks - and Lucky Strike, the closest public location-based-entertainment pure-play, told the market on 2026-08-27 that June was the single month that flipped its eleven-month positive cumulative into a negative full year, attributing it explicitly to the World Cup 'drawing consumers away' from its venues, with Q4 same-store sales at -2.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The sweep's own 'already in the wire' list carries the -4% commentary as the known quantity, which is exactly the problem: it is the anchor, and it was set before the tournament window it cannot describe. If the market had re-anchored on the peer disclosure, Q2 EPS consensus would visibly have moved after 2026-08-27 and the 15.84% event-implied move would not need to be that wide to cover a quarter management has supposedly already pre-announced most of. The range is wide and crosses zero deliberately: D&B is a sports bar with 40-foot screens that programmed the tournament nationally, so unlike a bowling operator it monetises the occasion that hurt the peer, and the sign for this specific name is genuinely two-sided.
findings.independence: Square's transaction data (via eMarketer, 2026-07-02) shows US bar and restaurant revenue up 8% in the opening round with 10pm-1am transactions +20.2%, and Colliers/Placer.ai found the lift was concentrated near match venues in the 11 host cities with 'minimal' gains across wider metros - so the drag is real outside host markets and D&B's ~230 domestic stores are national, not host-city weighted: https://www.emarketer.com/content/world-cup-bars-restaurants-sales-growth-2026

findings.finding: The leverage number the equity market quotes is not the covenant number: the Q1 FY2026 10-Q shows the $650m revolver with $150.0m drawn plus $20.5m of letters of credit - 26% usage, below the 35% threshold at which the financial covenant is tested at all - and the Fifth Amendment of December 2025 raised the maximum Net Total Leverage Ratio from 3.50x to 4.00x against a credit-agreement-defined ratio of 3.3x at 2026-05-05, versus the headline 4.7x net leverage that Debtwire and the sweep brief both carry.
findings.why_not_priced: The first-lien term loans yield 11.7-12.7% against a 7.26% single-B index and the equity's 25-delta skew is +6.18 - both are paying for a credit accident. But there is no 8-K covenant amendment, no Item 2.05 or 2.06, no Schedule 13D, no going-concern language and no restructuring-adviser news in the filing stream since the 2026-08-04 CEO 8-K; the only corporate action in the last six weeks is routine new-officer equity grants. If the covenant arithmetic were priced rather than the headline ratio, a print that simply shows the revolver flat or paid down through the seasonally strongest cash quarter would not be capable of removing a tail - and it is.
findings.independence: Debtwire's 1Q26 credit report (2026-08-03) independently confirms the mechanics - $499m liquidity comprising $20m cash and $480m revolver availability, and that the revolver covenant only requires total leverage under 4.0x 'if facility usage surpasses 35%': https://ionanalytics.com/insights/debtwire/dave-busters-turnaround-remains-unclear-as-underperformance-weighs-on-credit-profile-1q26-credit-report/

findings.finding: On 2026-08-31 - 27 days after the Q2 close, with the quarter's numbers in hand - the compensation committee made first-time officer grants to Amanda Busby as Chief Operations Officer (72,464 RSUs, 74,294 options and 55,741 performance shares, all struck at $8.97, shares owned after the grant equal to the grant) and to Derek Sample as Chief Accounting Officer (39,019 RSUs, 52,006 options, 39,019 performance shares), with the performance tranches keyed to same-store-sales metrics; the new CEO's 2026-08-10 award puts its first PSU tranche on H2 fiscal 2026 same-store-sales *growth* and its options on a 2x share-price hurdle.
findings.why_not_priced: Form 4s for a $283m-cap company are not covered, and nobody reads the grant date against the fiscal calendar. A board about to withdraw the year at a new CEO's first print does not, three weeks after that quarter closed, build out a COO and CAO bench and set tranche one of their long-term incentive on positive H2 comps and a doubled share price - it would defer the grant or reset the metric. If this were priced there would be a note referencing the 08-31 grant terms; there is none, and the stock fell further after them.
findings.independence: The 2026-08-04 8-K describing the CEO's award confirms the same structure from a different filing - three equal PSU tranches on same-store-sales growth targets for H2 2026, 2027 and 2028, and options earned only at 2x the stock price within three years: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001525769/000152576926000032/play-20260803.htm

searched_and_found_nothing: Placer.ai foot-traffic on Dave & Buster's: the two articles that surface (NRN 'foot traffic rose in Q2', Placer blog 'Ups Its Game') are dated 2024-09-05 and 2025-04-04 respectively - prior-year data served as current. No 2026-vintage D&B chain traffic series is public.

Topgolf as a Q2 read-through: the 'same venue sales -3%, traffic +6% in Q2 and +12% in July' figures returned by search are prior-year; Callaway divested Topgolf in H1 2026 and its 2026-08-04 release reports it as discontinued operations with no venue metrics. Dropped entirely.

KKR activist stake headlines: the PitchBook item is from 2022 (shares at $47.37). EDGAR shows no SC 13D or 13D/A since 2023-12-07 and no 13G since 2024-11-14. No activist, no strategic-alternatives process.
Restructuring/liability-management advisers, creditor groups or an exchange offer - nothing in news or the 8-K stream; no Item 2.05 or 2.06 filed.

Goodwill/tradename impairment as a kitchen-sink candidate: $742.6m goodwill and $178.2m tradenames against a $283m market cap and 13 straight negative-comp quarters make one plausible, but the Q1 10-Q carries both balances unchanged with no triggering-event or going-concern discussion, so there is no evidence it is coming and I did not size it.
Permanent store-closure programme - only a temporary LA County health closure at Ovation Hollywood (2026-03) and a new-store fill at Annapolis Mall; no closure list.
Current secondary marks on the June-2029 first-lien term loans; only the 2026-08-03 Debtwire yield range is public, so I cannot tell whether credit has moved since.
Current short interest as a percent of float - the figures returned carry a 2025-09-30 settlement date and are not usable.
'Dave & Buster's dials back confusing experience changes' - dated 2025-06-13, prior year.
Whether a permanent CFO has been named since Cory Hatton's interim appointment - no 8-K and no announcement.
baseline_tension: Net against the baseline: the +6.18 skew and the 18% run-down are paying for a credit accident that the covenant arithmetic and an empty 8-K stream do not support, and for a comp quarter whose single biggest exogenous driver just set a 132-year record in the company's favour - but my one genuinely negative finding, that the market's -4% comp anchor predates the World Cup window, agrees with the skew, which is why the sum is +2.0 and not larger.
